items.parentTitle: Complex Sentences, Subordinating Conjunctions, and Clauses
items.whatStudentsLearn: In Level 5 English, children learn how authors construct complex sentences using main clauses and dependent clauses (with conjunctions like 'although', 'despite', 'because', 'whereas') and use commas accurately to separate clauses.
items.whatThisMeans: Knowing how to craft sentences that show nuance and relationship, like: 'Although the rain was heavy, the match continued until sunset.'
items.whyItMatters: Sophisticated clause structure elevates student writing from basic storytelling to mature academic expression expected in Grade 5 NAPLAN and secondary school.

homeActivities.title: Clause Puzzle Builder
homeActivities.description: Start a sentence with a dependent clause ('Even though it was freezing cold outside...') and challenge your child to complete it with an interesting main clause.

items.parentTitle: Historical, Cultural, and Social Contexts in Literature
items.whatStudentsLearn: Students identify how texts reflect specific historical, cultural, and social contexts in literature by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors and a wide range of Australian and world authors.
items.whatThisMeans: Examining how a story's time period or cultural setting influences what characters value, how they talk, and what challenges they face.
items.whyItMatters: Builds historical perspective, cultural literacy, and deeper comprehension of literature.

homeActivities.title: Time-Travel Reading Chat
homeActivities.description: When reading a story set in the past or a different country, discuss what clues in the text tell you about how life was different back then.

items.parentTitle: Evaluating Arguments, Fact vs Opinion, and Point of View
items.whatStudentsLearn: Students analyse how texts are constructed for specific audiences and purposes, evaluating arguments, distinguishing fact from opinion, and identifying points of view.
items.whatThisMeans: Spotting whether a writer is presenting objective evidence or attempting to persuade readers using emotive language or selected facts.
items.whyItMatters: Vital for critical thinking, digital media evaluation, and writing convincing persuasive essays for NAPLAN.

homeActivities.title: Fact vs Claim Detector
homeActivities.description: Look at an advertisement or news headline together. Ask your child to point out one factual detail and one opinion or emotional claim.
